tweets.text: Dynamic workflows are useful for tasks that are too big for a single agent loop, such as service-wide bug hunts, large migrations, or stress-testing a design. They're powerful and can be expensive, consuming a lot of tokens fast. Start with a scoped task to get a feel for it.

tweets.text: Opus 4.8 defaults to high effort. For coding tasks, it spends similar tokens to the 4.7 default while delivering better performance. For difficult tasks and long-running async work, use xhigh. We’ve increased rate limits in Claude Code to accommodate the increased token usage.

articles.content: We Asked Grok Build 0.1 to Plan and Build a Webhook Service Kilo Blog Subscribe Sign in We Asked Grok Build 0.1 to Plan and Build a Webhook Service Darko May 28, 2026 1 1 Share xAI released Grok Build 0.1 as a new coding model priced at $1 per 1M input tokens and $2 per 1M output tokens with a 256K context window. We ran it through Kilo Code (the VS Code extension) on a real backend task to see how it handles planning, implementation, and the long tool-calling sequence in between. TL;DR: Grok Build 0.1 planned and built a working webhook delivery service in TypeScript, Bun, and SQLite for $1.65 total ($0.17 to plan, $1.48 to implement) at roughly 120 tokens per second, with zero tool-calling failures across the run. tweets.text: We're not going to pretend it was flawless. The get-by-id endpoint leaks the encrypted secret. Signature comparison isn't constant-time. Integration coverage is thin. These are 30-second code-review fixes, not a rewrite. We flagged all of them.

tweets.creator: @kilocode
tweets.text: Phase 2: we pointed it at its own plan in Code Mode. 26 files. 3 tables. Real Drizzle migrations. AES-GCM encrypted secrets. SSRF guard. Non-destructive replay. The plan it wrote was the plan it executed. No drift, no quiet downgrades.

tweets.creator: @kilocode
tweets.text: First thing it did was open a web search. Pulled Stripe's signature format, GitHub's retry behavior, the Standard Webhooks spec. Then asked 9 clarifying questions before writing a single line. Framework, retry policy, secret storage, demo structure. The choices that actually shape the architecture.

tweets.creator: @kilocode
